writeup: TIC 468210255 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 6.7064 days and a primary eclipse depth of 6.93% dimming. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a secondary eclipse at 7.4 sigma significance, with a detection signal-to-noise ratio of 110.0 from the Box Least Squares method. Pixel-level image analysis confirmed a signal peak with signal-to-noise of 47.2, though the centroid offset of 3.1 arcsec from the target raises an important concern: the detection margin between this star and a nearby bright companion is only 0.064 pixels, falling within TESS's known centroid uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels. This means TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate the two objects, leaving open the question of whether the dimming actually originates from TIC 468210255 or its neighbor.
